Subject: Re: Clarify pricing for multi-site private deployment

Hi Caroline — great questions. Quick high-level framing below, happy to jump on a call to walk through numbers tomorrow.

Option A — Site-based (recommended for multi-site parity):
- Per-site operator license (covers control plane/operator per physical location).
- Platform fee applied once per customer (not per site) and amortized for pilot conversion.
- Pilot: full platform fee waived for first 3 months, operator licenses reduced by 50% for pilot sites.
- Production: operator license at full list, platform fee reactivates pro rata across committed sites.

Pros: predictable fixed cost per site, easier for compliance and firewalled environments.
Cons: can be suboptimal if your long-term density is very high at a single site.

Option B — Seat/node (per-GPU/node) pricing:
- Charge per inferred GPU seat (consumption-adjacent), lower up-front but scales with density.
- Platform fee applies once customer-wide; pilot credits can be applied against first three invoice cycles.

Pros: aligns cost with usage; good when site density varies.
Cons: less predictable for procurement; more metering.

SRE retainer: optional 3-month retainer (monthly rate) or an hourly on-call block. We can append to the SOW as add-on line item.

I'll attach a quick sketch that maps your site sizes to both models for transparency. If you want, we can propose a hybrid: site-license for low-density sites, seat pricing for the high-density site, with a one-time pilot credit that converts to a production credit on signature.

Best,
